Article Title: The role of advanced manufacturing technologies in delivering energy-efficient appliances
Article Text:
The manufacturing engine behind efficiency

From factory floor to energy savings

A sustainability dividend

India's manufacturing moment

Looking ahead

-- Ajay DD Singhania, Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer, EPACK Durable Limited

India's relationship with home comfort is undergoing a significant shift. Rapid urbanisation, rising disposable incomes, and increasingly extreme summers have pushed air conditioners and other home appliances from aspirational purchases to household essentials. As per recent research reports, India's room air conditioner market is expected to grow at a double-digit pace of over 14% through 2034, with similar momentum witnessed across washing machines, refrigerators, and other durables. But there is a quieter, equally important shift happening alongside this demand boom, where consumers are no longer asking only "does it cool well?" They are asking "how much will it cost me to run, and what does it cost the planet?"Energy efficiency has moved from a niche concern to a mainstream purchase driver. Star ratings, once fine print, are now a headline feature. Inverter technology, which adjusts compressor speed to match cooling needs rather than switching on and off at full power, has gone from premium add-on to near-default expectation. This shift in consumer priorities is reshaping what manufacturers must deliver, and increasingly, the answer lies not just in product design, but in how products are made.There is a popular misconception that energy efficiency is purely an engineering or R&D outcome.For instance, a smarter compressor here or a better refrigerant there. However, even the most impressive design blueprint is only as efficient as the factory that builds it and this is where advanced manufacturing technologies are quietly changing the consumer durables sector.In the same vein, automation and robotics on assembly lines are improving the precision with which components are placed, fitted, and sealed, which are critical for appliances where even minor tolerances in heat exchangers, refrigerant lines, or motor windings can give way to measurable energy losses. Smart manufacturing systems embedded with sensors and real-time monitoring ensures that every unit coming off the line meets exacting specifications. Moreover, AI-driven production planning is helping factories anticipate demand fluctuations and optimise output without the waste that comes from overproduction or rushed retrofits.Additionally, digital quality control using machine vision, automated leak testing, and data-logged performance checks has replaced much of the manual inspection that once introduced variability into the manufacturing process. Industry 4.0 arriving in appliance factories, and it is reshaping the relationship between manufacturing excellence and product performance.The link between manufacturing precision and energy outcomes is direct. The Economic Survey 2025-26 showcases that medium- and high-technology industries now contribute 46.3% of India’s manufacturing value added, indicating a shift towards more sophisticated production structure. Better-integrated compressors run with less friction loss, precisely wound motors consume less power for the same output, and accurately calibrated heat exchangers transfer thermal energy more effectively, thereby reducing the load on the system. None of this is possible through design alone, rather, it requires manufacturing processes capable of translating engineering intent into physical reality, unit after unit, at volumes running into millions.The benefits extend beyond the appliances themselves as automated manufacturing reduces material wastage through optimised cutting, moulding, and assembly processes. Smart resource utilisation inside factories and leaner supply chains are lowering the environmental footprint of production itself. In a country working toward ambitious sustainability and climate commitments, energy-efficient manufacturing processes are becoming as important as energy-efficient commodities.This technological shift is unfolding at a pivotal time for India as Government initiatives such as Make in India and the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme have catalysed investment in domestic appliance manufacturing, further strengthened by the Union Budget 2026–27's increase in the outlay for the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) to ₹40,000 crore, alongside expanded PLI support for white goods. As local supply chains mature, India is positioning itself not just as a market for appliances, but as a veritable global manufacturing hub, with growing export potential to markets across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East.This is a meaningful opportunity. The countries that win in consumer durables manufacturing over the next decade will be those that pair scale with sophistication and high-volume output, without compromising on precision or efficiency.The next phase of this journey will be defined by smart, connected factories and facilities where AI, IoT sensors, predictive maintenance, and digital twins work together to anticipate faults before they occur, optimise energy use in real time, and continuously improve product quality. Manufacturing will increasingly be judged not just on output volumes, but on its contribution to sustainability and efficiency outcomes.The future of consumer durables will be defined not only by product innovation but also by manufacturing innovation. Advanced manufacturing technologies will play a critical role in enabling the production of energy-efficient, high-quality, and sustainable appliances at scale. As India strengthens its position as a global manufacturing hub, investments in technology, automation, and innovation will be key to delivering the next generation of consumer appliances.
Article Summary: India's room air conditioner market is expected to grow at a double-digit pace of over 14% through 2034. Smart manufacturing systems embedded with sensors and real-time monitoring ensures that every unit coming off the line meets exacting specifications. AI-driven production planning is helping factories anticipate demand fluctuations.

Article Title: Mercedes-Benz may get 'banned' from selling vehicles in America, and reason is China
Article Text:
What Mercedes-Benz said on the bill



Bill to hit some European car makers too



German automaker Mercedes-Benz may become the unlikely casualty of an upcoming US legislation. This comes after the US Senate Commerce Committee approved a legislation to toughen a government ban on Chinese automakers entering the American market. This restriction on Chinese companies could also bar Mercedes-Benz from selling its vehicles in the United States of America. As per the bill's provisions, it seeks to ban companies with more than 15% ownership by Chinese entities, which means that it would also bar Mercedes-Benz because of its nearly 20% passive Chinese investment.Called Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026, the bill passed unanimously, setting it up for consideration by the full Senate. The bill has been proposed by Senator Moreno. Praising the passage of his bipartisan bill, Moreno said, "Connected Vehicle Security Act protects American automakers and workers from the dire threat of Chinese automobiles by banning them and their connected components on American soil. This bill prohibits the import, sale, and operation of vehicles manufactured in China, or any other country of concern, and bans the use of Chinese-developed connected vehicle technologies, such as software and data systems, on America roads."Moreno, an Ohio Republican, said that Mercedes-Benz would have until 2030 to comply and could get waivers if needed from the ownership requirement if necessary. Incidentally, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, cellular connectivity and some satellite communications technologies too are covered under the rules based on national security concerns linked to the ability of vehicles to collect sensitive data on American owners.Senators Moreno and Elissa Slotkin, a Democrat, proposed the legislation to codify a regulation imposed by the Biden administration that effectively bans all Chinese automakers from selling passenger vehicles in the US and takes other steps to prevent China from entering the US light-duty market. "We're preventing an absolute, total, and complete destruction of our industrial base," Moreno said as per the report.Senator Ted Cruz, the chair of the committee, claimed that General Motors was pushing for the provision to get Mercedes-Benz out of the market and make its Cadillac brand more competitive. He said "we would never consider" banning Mercedes-Benz sales in the United States. Responding to Cruz's claim GM said that the legislation isn't about any individual automaker and added the automaker "supports policies that protect and strengthen American manufacturing and the global competitiveness of US automakers. "Moreno added that GM plans to shift production of its Chinese-made Buick Envision to the United States for the 2028 model year and said Ford has agreed to move Chinese-made Lincolns to the United States. "I view that as a big victory," Moreno said.He further told Reuters that Google's self-driving unit Waymo, which had been talking with Chinese automaker Geely about platforms coming from China, "has committed to looking at a Detroit-based manufacturer for their future platforms."Responding to the bill, Mercedes-Benz pointed to its extensive operations in the US. The company further said that it "continues to support legislation designed to protect US national security. Mercedes-Benz also remains committed to ensuring that any legislation does not impact our operations. The company will continue to safeguard its employees, dealers, suppliers, and customers."Mercedes-Benz is not the only automaker to be hit by the upcoming legislation. Last month, electric-vehicle maker Polestar claimed that the Trump administration was forcing the company to stop selling vehicles in the US beginning in the 2027 model year. The Sweden-based company is majority-owned by China's Geely Holding.Polestar's sister brand and co-founder, Volvo Cars, said in May that it received authorization to keep selling vehicles in the US, though it said it still must meet the rule's requirements.
Article Summary: The US Senate Commerce Committee approved a legislation to toughen a government ban on Chinese automakers entering the American market. This restriction on Chinese companies could also bar Mercedes-Benz from selling its vehicles in the United States of America. As per the bill's provisions, it seeks to ban companies with more than 15% ownership by Chinese entities.

Article Title: Why China's biggest memory chip maker CXMT that made Apple seek 'special permission' from the US government is 'scaring' Chinese investors
Article Text:
CXMT is China’s biggest memory chip maker

Why investors are worried about CXMT's IPO





Analysts say CXMT's IPO is adding to market pressure

China’s biggest memory chip maker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has become one of the most closely watched companies in the country's semiconductor industry. The chipmaker, which reportedly made Apple seek special permission from the US government before considering its memory chips for some products due to US export restrictions, is now making headlines for its massive $8.6 billion Shanghai IPO. Likely to be Asia’s largest IPO of 2026, the upcoming IPO is raising concerns that it could drain money from China's stock market. According to a report by CNBC, investors are selling other technology shares to free up cash for the highly anticipated listing, adding pressure on Chinese semiconductor stocks and the broader technology sector.CXMT is expected to debut on Shanghai's STAR Market on July 27 after raising $8.6 billion through its initial public offering. Market experts, quoted in the CNBC report, say the listing is creating fears of a short-term liquidity squeeze because investors are moving money out of existing stocks to buy CXMT shares.Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, said investors expect CXMT's market value to quickly cross 1 trillion yuan ($139 billion) after listing. "Once it passes 1 trillion yuan, CXMT will become a primary heavyweight in the STAR Market and semiconductor indices, forcing index funds, active funds, and sector-specific funds to reallocate toward it," Sun said.As a result, investors are reducing holdings in sectors that previously led the market rally, including memory chip makers, semiconductor equipment companies and domestic chip suppliers. The STAR 50 Index, which tracks the largest technology companies listed on Shanghai's STAR Market, has fallen nearly 20% this quarter.Peter Alexander, founder of Z-Ben Advisors, said there is "no question" that money is being pulled from the secondary market ahead of CXMT's public listing. He expects strong demand when trading begins, saying the stock could see a sharp jump during its first two days before both the shares and the broader market stabilize.However, analysts said the IPO is not the main reason behind the recent weakness in Chinese technology stocks.Sun said crowded investor positions and high leverage in China's technology sector remain the biggest reasons for the pullback. He added that weakness in South Korean semiconductor stocks has also weighed on global chip valuations and encouraged profit-taking in China.Benjamin Cavender, managing director at CMR Consulting, described CXMT as more of a catalyst than the original cause of the selloff. He said the situation resembles the "cash call" effect often seen before major IPOs, when investors sell existing holdings to raise cash for new listings.
Article Summary: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) is China's biggest memory chip maker. It is expected to debut on Shanghai's STAR Market on July 27 after raising $8.6 billion through its initial public offering. Market experts say the listing is creating fears of a short-term liquidity squeeze.

Article Title: Tesla sees 'Worst Day' since the day Elon Musk said that 'I can’t pass a TV without spotting a Tesla up in flames'
Article Text:
Why Elon Musk lost $18.6 billion in a single day

Tesla plans to spend more on AI

Elon Musk avoids merger speculation

Elon Musk’s net worth dropped by $18.6 billion on July 23 after Tesla shares dropped by 14%, marking its largest single-day decline since June 5, 2025. According to Forbes Billionaires List, the drop in Tesla stock lowered Elon Musk’s net worth to $731.7 billion. Despite the fall, he remains the world’s richest person ahead of Google co-founder Larry Page ($263.8 billion) and Amazon’s Jeff Bezos ($245.4 billion). The drop comes days after Musk said “I can’t pass a TV without spotting a Tesla up in flames.” He was then talking about the widespread protests at Tesla showrooms and vandalism of the vehicles.Tesla shares plunged after the company reported quarterly results that missed profit expectations despite beating revenue estimates. The car maker posted revenue of $28.2 billion, above analysts' estimate of $27.2 billion, according to FactSet. However, earnings came in at 33 cents per share, well below the expected 55 cents per share.As per a Forbes article, the weak profit numbers, combined with Tesla's plans to continue spending heavily on AI, weighed on investor sentiment.During the earnings call, Tesla Chief Financial Officer Vaibhav Taneja said the company still expects to spend $25 billion this year, with even higher investments planned in the coming years.The spending is aimed at supporting Tesla's AI ambitions, including its Optimus humanoid robot and robotaxi business.However, analysts said investors now want to see clear progress rather than promises.Morgan Stanley analysts said the spending is a "necessary investment" but added that Tesla must deliver "tangible" milestones for its robotaxi and Optimus projects.Canaccord Genuity analysts also said they expect meaningful robotaxi deployments over the next six months as Tesla expands its AI strategy.During the earnings call, Elon Musk was also asked about speculation surrounding a possible merger between Tesla and SpaceX. The tech billionaire declined to comment on combining the two companies, saying such discussions cannot happen during an earnings call. However, Musk acknowledged there is "more and more overlap" between the businesses, pointing to Starlink connectivity in Cybertrucks and the proposed TeraFab AI chip manufacturing venture involving Tesla and SpaceX.
Article Summary: Elon Musk’s net worth dropped by $18.6 billion on July 23 after Tesla shares dropped by 14%, marking its largest single-day decline since June 5, 2025. According to Forbes Billionaires List, the drop in Tesla stock lowered Elon Musk's net worth to $731.7 billion. The drop comes days after Musk said “I can’t pass a TV without spotting a Tesla up in flames”

Article Title: NASA has grown plants in space for years: New research says the next step is growing medicines, starting with a tobacco and a virus
Article Text:
How UC San Diego grew cowpea mosaic virus on tobacco and black-eyed pea plants in simulated microgravity

Blood clots, cut-short missions and why medical emergencies on the ISS make Mars pharmaceuticals urgent

Astronauts heading to Mars will be gone for roughly 400 days, and everything they need has to travel with them or arrive ahead of them. Food is the problem everyone talks about. The bigger one might be the medicine cabinet. More than half the pharmaceuticals stocked on the International Space Station expire within three years—well short of the window a Mars crew would need them for. Expired drugs aren't just weaker. They can turn toxic.A new study out of the University of California San Diego proposes a workaround that sounds almost absurdly simple: grow the medicine on the way. Researchers cultivated a plant virus with therapeutic properties in a lab setup engineered to mimic microgravity, and the results suggest astronauts could one day farm their own pharmaceuticals mid-flight instead of watching a supply cabinet slowly go bad.The virus in question is cowpea mosaic virus, or CPMV, which has shown promise in prompting the human immune system to attack cancer cells. The UC San Diego team grew it on two hosts—Nicotiana benthamiana, a cousin of the tobacco plant, and Vigna unguiculata no. 5, better known as the black-eyed pea. The pea plant is the interesting one. It grows the virus and produces edible food, which makes it a two-for-one on a spacecraft where every square centimetre is contested.To simulate weightlessness, the plants sat on a random positioning machine that tumbled in three dimensions, driven by a custom Python script running on a Raspberry Pi. Harvesting was the clever part. Instead of destroying the plant, engineers pulled apoplastic fluid from the leaves using a vacuum, then spun it in a centrifuge to isolate the viral extract. The ISS already has a lab-grade centrifuge on board.They have already happened. A NASA astronaut was found to have a blood clot during a routine ultrasound in 2018 and was put on enoxaparin to prevent a pulmonary embolism. More recently, astronaut Mike Fincke's medical emergency cut his ISS mission short. Motion sickness, headaches, and urinary tract infections are routine. On Mars, there is no early return flight—only what the crew can grow.
Article Summary: UC San Diego grew cowpea mosaic virus on tobacco and black-eyed pea plants in simulated microgravity. The results suggest astronauts could one day farm their own pharmaceuticals mid-flight. More than half the pharmaceuticals stocked on the International Space Station expire within three years.

Article Title: ‘AI ending humanity is complete nonsense’: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang challenges fellow tech CEOs on doomsday scenario
Article Text:
Jensen Huang (File Image)

Silicon Valley divided over existential risk



Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has issued a rebuke against widespread ‘AI doomsday’ warnings, dismissing catastrophic claims that artificial intelligence (AI) will destroy civilization or trigger mass unemployment. In an interview with Axios, Huang warned that scaring workers, businesses and lawmakers away from adopting AI poses a far greater economic danger than the technology itself.“The fact that this is going to be the end of humanity — it's complete nonsense. The fact that this is going to destroy half of the American jobs is complete nonsense,” Huang was quoted as saying.Huang’s comments stand in stark contrast to warnings issued by other prominent AI leaders and industry pioneers. Previously, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated AI could “most likely lead to the end of the world” and co-signed a public declaration urging global leaders to treat AI extinction risks with urgency.Anthropic’s Dario Amodei has been most vocal about the negative effects of the technology. He has repeatedly cautioned that rapid AI training trajectories could lead to massive job displacement and potentially catastrophic outcomes for humanity.Elon Musk has also been warning of severe societal risks and calling for pauses on unchecked AI deployment.Huang’s intervention arrives as Washington aims to balance two major AI policy challenges: establishing domestic guardrails for powerful models while preventing overly restrictive rules that could handicap US tech giants.Huang argues that overreacting to hypothetical extinction scenarios risks suffocating practical innovation across medical diagnostics, scientific research and enterprise automation. He said that instead of restricting technology out of fear, America must push forward aggressively to maintain its competitive edge on the global stage.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang dismisses claims that artificial intelligence will destroy civilization or trigger mass unemployment. He argues that scaring workers, businesses and lawmakers away from adopting AI poses a far greater economic danger than the technology itself. His comments stand in stark contrast to warnings issued by other prominent AI leaders and industry pioneers.

Article Title: IIRIS Consulting acquires publicly-listed fintech company Dion Global Solutions
Article Text: IIRIS Consulting (Indus IntelliRisk and IntelliSense Services Private Limited) has acquired Dion Global Solutions Limited, a publicly listed fintech company. The acquisition follows the approval of IIRIS's resolution plan by the National Company Law Tribunal on 21 July 2026.The acquisition marks IIRIS's entry into the listed company space and gives its IntelliFuture suite of AI-enabled products an immediate route to market. Dion's customer base includes HDFC Bank , Canara Bank, Sharekhan, JM Financial, Indiabulls Ventures, IIFL, Jhaveri Securities, Equitas Small Finance Bank and BgSE Financials Limited.Under the terms of the resolution plan, which carries a total value of Rs 802.93 lakh, IIRIS has infused fresh capital into Dion Global through the subscription of 50,00,000 equity shares of Rs 10 each. The acquisition gives IIRIS a listed platform and an installed base across India’s banking and capital markets ecosystem, and the firm intends to invest further in Dion’s technology, people and product roadmap as the combined business scales.Garry Singh, President, IIRIS Consulting, said, “Every conversation we have with a bank, a broker or a wealth manager today is about digitisation. Institutions want risk, compliance and case management to run on technology rather than on paper, and IIRIS made a deliberate decision to build for that shift.This acquisition positions us exactly where the market is heading. We move from being a risk firm that built technology to a technology company with three decades of financial markets infrastructure under its roof. ”At the centre of the combined offering is the IntelliFuture suite, a family of seven AI-enabled products built from IIRIS’s investigation and risk experience.Sagarika Chakraborty, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer, IIRIS Consulting, said, “IIRIS built its name on investigations, forensic intelligence and risk advisory delivered as a service, and we converted that experience into the IntelliFuture suite of AI-enabled products covering fraud classification, case tracking, asset tracing and risk visibility. Dion completes the picture. Its platforms already sit inside more than 250 banks, brokers and wealth managers, which means the intelligence we once delivered as reports can now live as a capability inside our clients' own systems. Our immediate focus is a seamless transition for Dion's clients and employees.”IIRIS also brings an international footprint, with offices and products deployed across Middle East, Europe and Asia.
Article Summary: IIRIS has infused fresh capital into Dion Global through the subscription of 50,00,000 equity shares of Rs 10 each. The acquisition gives IIRIS a listed platform and an installed base across India’s banking and capital markets ecosystem.

Article Title: Swiggy, Zepto, Meesho deposit Karnataka gig welfare fee
Article Text: Eternal, Zepto, Swiggy, Urban Company and Meesho have deposited the welfare fee mandated under Karnataka’s gig-worker law, even as the companies continue to challenge the legislation in the high court.The platforms deposited the money following a Karnataka High Court direction, industry body Internet and Mobile Association of India said on Thursday. It did not disclose the amount paid by the companies.The law seeks to create a state-run fund for the social security and welfare of people working through delivery, ride-hailing, home-service and other digital platforms. It also introduces worker registration, grievance-redressal and transparency requirements for platforms.Earlier this month, the high court declined to stay the law but protected the companies from coercive action for the time being. It asked them to deposit their disputed second-quarter welfare contributions with the court. The money will remain separate until the case is decided.The platforms have argued that Karnataka’s requirements overlap with the Centre’s Code on Social Security and could result in companies paying twice towards gig-worker welfare.The state government has maintained that the two laws do not conflict.IAMAI said the companies were seeking “harmonisation” between the central and state frameworks to avoid duplication and ensure that “every rupee contributed translates into maximum benefit for gig workers.”The platforms said they already fund accident and health insurance, maternity assistance, emergency support and programmes that help workers access credit. Collectively, their initiatives cover a broader pool of more than six million monthly active platform workers across India, according to IAMAI.Meesho, which was separately questioned about the law during its June-quarter analyst call, said it had already accounted for the potential financial impact. “From a conservative standpoint, we continue to make provisions and provide for any of those costs into our P&L,” Meesho management said. This means its reported expenses already factor in the possibility that it may eventually have to bear the fee.“There shouldn’t be any adverse impact if we are required to pay it,” management said, adding that the amounts involved were “not material in nature.”Under the state’s current fee structure, platforms must contribute 50 paise for a delivery made using a two-wheeler, 75 paise for a three-wheeler and Re 1 for a four-wheeler, the Karnataka government told the court. The case is scheduled to be heard again on July 31.
Article Summary: Eternal, Zepto, Swiggy, Urban Company and Meesho have deposited the welfare fee mandated under Karnataka’s gig-worker law. The companies continue to challenge the legislation in the high court. The law seeks to create a state-run fund for the social security and welfare of people working through delivery, ride- hailing, home-service and other digital platforms.

Article Title: Swiggy board clears 49.5% foreign ownership cap
Article Text: Swiggy’s board on Thursday approved a proposal to cap foreign ownership in the company at 49.5%, making its most concrete move yet toward becoming an Indian-owned and controlled company.The proposal will go to shareholders at Swiggy’s annual general meeting on August 18. It will need approval through a special resolution.The cap will apply to total foreign ownership on a fully diluted basis. This includes foreign portfolio investors, non-resident Indians, and Indian companies or investment vehicles that are themselves foreign-owned or controlled.The move comes weeks after Swiggy told stock exchanges that foreign investment in the company stood at 49.76% as of July 6. At the time, the company said the number did not, by itself, change its ownership, control, management, voting rights or shareholder rights.That earlier disclosure was only a snapshot. In a listed company, foreign ownership can move up or down as shares trade. The latest proposal is different. If shareholders approve it, Swiggy will have a formal guardrail to stop foreign ownership from moving beyond 49.5%.The company is also seeking changes to its Articles of Association.Swiggy said these changes are part of its broader effort to qualify as an Indian-owned and controlled company under foreign exchange laws. The proposed changes include removing some existing individual and institutional nomination rights and revising nomination rights for specified resident individuals.This is important because Indian-owned and controlled status depends on two things: who owns the company and who controls it. Ownership is linked to shareholding. Control can also depend on board seats, nomination rights, voting rights and shareholder agreements.For Swiggy, the larger issue is quick commerce. India’s foreign investment rules allow foreign-funded e-commerce companies to run marketplaces. But they restrict inventory-led e-commerce, where the platform owns goods and sells them directly to customers.This does not mean Swiggy immediately plans to move Instamart to an inventory-led model. The company has not said so. But an Indian-owned and controlled structure could give the group more flexibility over how it organises sourcing, inventory and investments across subsidiaries.Swiggy’s move follows a similar step by Eternal, the parent of Zomato and Blinkit. Eternal shareholders last year approved a 49.5% foreign ownership cap to preserve its domestic status. A Nishith Desai Associates note said the move was aimed at keeping flexibility for Blinkit and avoiding the risk of Zomato’s investment into Blinkit being treated as indirect foreign investment.
Article Summary: The proposal will go to shareholders at Swiggy’s annual general meeting on August 18. It will need approval through a special resolution. This includes foreign portfolio investors, non-resident Indians, and Indian companies or investment vehicles that are themselves foreign-owned or controlled.

Article Title: This 16-year-old Canadian student built an AI robot turtle that hunts plastic invisible to the eye, and won $50,000 for it
Article Text:
Evan Budz, 16, with the autonomous bionic sea turtle robot that uses AI and an underwater holographic camera to detect microplastics in lakes — the project that won him a $50,000 scholarship at the 2026 Regeneron ISEF.

Robot turtle inspired by a snapping turtle on an Ontario camping trip

AI microplastic detection at 10 microns: how the holographic camera works

Why microplastic lab testing is slow and expensive, and what this robot changes

A 16-year-old student from Ontario, Canada has built a robotic sea turtle that swims on its own, dives to a set depth, and uses AI to spot microplastics floating in lakes and oceans. Evan Budz won a $50,000 scholarship for the project at the 2026 Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair in May, taking home the Gordon E. Moore Award for Positive Outcomes for Future Generations.The machine did not start out impressive. Budz's first prototype went straight to the bottom of his grandparents' backyard pool in Canada. He described it sinking like a brick, unable to swim or hold its depth. That was the summer of 2024, and it took roughly 2,000 hours of building to get the robot working, plus another 2,000 on the underwater holographic camera mounted on its shell.The idea came from a snapping turtle Budz watched while camping with his family earlier that year. He was struck by how fluid the movement was, and decided to build something that copied it. Turtles turned out to be a practical choice beyond the aesthetics.They are efficient swimmers, which matters for long missions where recharging is not an option. They are also large enough to carry sensors and imaging gear inside the shell, and common enough across aquatic environments that other organisms are not spooked by them.To get the motion right, Budz studied research literature and video, then consulted staff at Ripley's Aquarium about how green sea turtle flippers actually generate thrust. The flippers were designed in CAD, 3D-printed, and driven by a custom multi-axis servo mechanism that changes the angle of attack between upstroke and downstroke. Computational fluid dynamics simulations refined the shape before any of it hit the water. A spherical dome on the front of the chassis cut drag by 65% compared with a flat endcap.Depth control runs on a variable ballast system built from a linear servo and two syringes, with a pressure sensor feeding a PID loop. In testing between 20 and 150 cm, it held its target depth within 5 cm. A 9-axis inertial measurement unit handles heading, and the robot completed three-pass and four-pass grid searches in a 4x5 m pool with tracking error under 5 degrees.The detection side is where the AI comes in. Budz started building the holographic imaging system in the summer of 2025, and the hard part was tuning the hardware to resolve particles as small as 10 microns and tell plastic apart from small organisms. By the time ISEF came around, the system was hitting 94% accuracy on that distinction.Budz calls the standard process convoluted. Samples go to a laboratory, analysis takes days even for small batches, and it costs money. None of that works in a remote lake with no lab and no trained technicians nearby. His robot analyses the water where it swims.The Ocean Conservancy estimates 11 million metric tons of plastic waste reach the ocean every year, affecting more than 1,300 marine species. Over 1,700 students competed at this year's ISEF, which handed out more than $7 million in total. Budz plans to put the scholarship toward a university degree in science or engineering.
Article Summary: Evan Budz, 16, from Ontario, Canada has built a robotic sea turtle that swims on its own, dives to a set depth, and uses AI to spot microplastics floating in lakes and oceans. He won a $50,000 scholarship for the project at the 2026 Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair.

Article Title: After accusing Kimi K3 AI model maker Moonshot AI of ‘stealing’ Anthropic's Fable model, Scott Bessent warns Chinese companies of ‘Entity List designations’
Article Text:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warns Chinese companies of Entity List designation

‘Moonshot AI used Nvidia chips to train models’



Read full post by Michael Kratsios on X



We have information that Moonshot AI distilled Anthropic’s Fable for the development of its K3 model.

To do this they developed a sophisticated internal platform to conduct large scale distillation against U.S. models, allowing them to quickly switch between multiple methods of access to avoid detection. Moonshot AI has also acquired GB300-equipped servers and has accessed GB300s in Thailand, likely to train its AI models.

The United States strongly supports the free and fair development of AI, including a thriving competitive ecosystem that spans frontier models, specialized systems, open-source frameworks, and open-weight models. Legitimate AI distillation used to create smaller, more efficient models plays a vital role in this open innovation ecosystem. However, large-scale, covert industrial distillation aimed at stealing proprietary U.S. technology and undermining American research is unacceptable.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has warned Kimi K3 AI model maker Moonshot AI and other Chinese AI companies of ‘Entity List’ designations after accusing them of using outputs from American frontier models, and saying that the officials have identified ‘evidence of US Al models appearing in some Chinese systems’.“We support open-source AI and the innovation it unlocks. But open source is not open season on American IP. When PRC firms conduct covert, industrial-scale distillation attacks that cross the line into IP theft, sanctions and Entity List designations will be on the table,” Bessent said in a post on X.US Entity List is a trade restriction tool that consists of groups that the US thinks are acting against the country’s national security. It also restricts sensitive technology exports and requires special government licenses.Bessent’s comments came soon after a senior White House official has accused Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) startup Moonshot AI of illegally tapping into restricted Nvidia chips to train its new AI model that the company claimed is as powerful as Anthropic’s Fable 5. The allegations follow Moonshot’s release of Kimi K3, a massive open-source model with 2.8 trillion parameters.The model has sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley after closing the performance gap with top American AI systems.Michael Kratsios, Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, publicly raised the alarm, accusing the Chinese company of circumventing strict US export controls to access Nvidia's high-end hardware abroad.Under current US trade restrictions, Nvidia’s most advanced AI semiconductors are strictly banned from being exported to China. While the US has permitted the use and sale of lower-powered chips, the high-performance Nvidia GB300 systems fall under tight restrictions due to their importance in training large-scale neural networks.
Article Summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warns Chinese companies of ‘Entity List’ designations. US officials have identified ‘evidence of US Al models appearing in some Chinese systems’ Moonshot AI has also acquired GB300-equipped servers and has accessed GB300s in Thailand, likely to train its models.

Article Title: Meesho bets lower prices will power growth as delivery costs fall
Article Text: Meesho expects products on its marketplace to become more affordable as it cuts delivery costs and passes most of those savings to sellers and shoppers, even as higher fuel prices and wages push up expenses across the ecommerce industry.The value-focused ecommerce platform said its cost per delivered order fell by about Re 1 sequentially in the June quarter. This was despite an increase in fuel costs and minimum wages in some states.“You should anticipate that we will continue to reduce our logistics cost at a very good pace,” founder and CEO Vidit Aatrey told analysts on Thursday. “Changes in fuel prices as well as minimum wages are going to be small blips in that entire picture.”Meesho’s average order value declined about 2% from a year earlier. The company said this was a smaller fall than usual because higher raw-material and delivery costs temporarily lifted prices. Over time, it expects average order values to decline by roughly 5% annually as efficiencies make lower-priced transactions viable.“As we start gaining more efficiencies and passing some of those on to customers, we will resume on the trajectory of average order values becoming lower,” CFO Dhiresh Bansal added.The strategy is central to Meesho’s pitch to value-conscious consumers, many of whom are first-time or relatively new online shoppers. The company competes with larger ecommerce platforms that have also sharpened their focus on goods priced below Rs 1,000.Aatrey said the competitive environment had always been intense and had not changed materially after recent moves by rivals. “People have launched sub-platforms to compete with us over the last many years,” he said. “Our pricing is getting better, our selection is getting better, and we continue to see good growth as well as cohort retention.”Meesho’s revenues rose 45% to Rs 3,826 crore in the June quarter, while its losses narrowed 54% to Rs 133 crore. Net merchandise value, or the value of goods sold after cancellations and returns, increased 34% to Rs 11,614 crore.The Bengaluru-based company had 274 million annual transacting users, up 29% from a year earlier. Orders placed during the quarter also rose 29% to 725 million.Valmo, Meesho’s logistics network, continued to handle roughly half of its shipments. The company said it allocates deliveries lane by lane to whichever partner offers the lowest cost, rather than trying to raise Valmo’s share for its own sake.“The ultimate share of Valmo would depend on all of these factors,” Bansal said. “The direction of the cost per delivered order would continue to come down. That is the objective with which we work.”The company plans to retain gains from advertising as profit, while passing a large part of future logistics savings back through lower prices. About two-thirds of sellers contributing to Meesho’s merchandise value already advertise on the platform. Management expects this share to increase as more sellers compete for visibility.Meesho maintained its longer-term expectation of about 25% annual growth in merchandise value over five years. It said growth would likely be faster in the initial years and moderate later.
Article Summary: Meesho expects products on its marketplace to become more affordable as it cuts delivery costs. The value-focused ecommerce platform said its cost per delivered order fell by about Re 1 sequentially. This was despite an increase in fuel costs and minimum wages in some states.

Article Title: In 1960, IMAX technology changed cinema; now Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey can be seen in true 70mm format at only 41 theatres worldwide because of this 50-year-old 'machine problem'
Article Text:
Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey is available in limited 70mm IMAX theaters worldwide. This scarcity stems from aging technology and the lack of new projector manufacturing. IMAX must rebuild and retrofit its old machines, which are large and complex. The film prints themselves are also massive, weighing hundreds of pounds. This combination restricts screenings to only forty-one global locations.

The

Odyssey

Variety

“There’s certainly more demand. The problem is they haven’t made new IMAX film projectors in about 50 years. So we retrofit them [and] rebuild them, and part of our strategy is to see how far we can take it.”

The Odyssey

A technology that dates back to the 1960s

Why replacing these projectors isn't easy

“Simply put, a 15/70mm projector isn’t just another mechanical assembly you can spin up on a modern production line in a factory somewhere. It’s a bespoke engineering solution to a bespoke physical problem, and that solution was designed for, and built in, a manufacturing era that ended decades ago.”

The film reels are equally demanding

The Odyssey

The Odyssey

Christopher Nolan'sis playing in IMAX cinemas worldwide, but viewers wanting to watch the film in its intended 70mm IMAX format have only 41 theatres to choose from. The reason is not limited demand or a marketing strategy, but a decades-old technology challenge: IMAX has not manufactured new 70mm film projectors for around 50 years, leaving the company to rebuild and retrofit ageing machines.Explaining the shortage, IMAX CEO Richard Gelfond recently toldThe scarcity means only a small number of theatres globally can screenin true 70mm IMAX format.IMAX is often associated with modern blockbusters, but the technology was developed in the late 1960s. Most cinemas have gone digital over the years, and the number of venues that could show large-format 70mm IMAX film has slowly dwindled.Today, most IMAX theatres use dual 2K digital projectors with a 1.90:1 aspect ratio, which are comparatively easier to manufacture and maintain. By contrast, 15/70mm IMAX projectors are specialised mechanical systems built for large-format film and require dedicated infrastructure to operate.The machines themselves are considerably larger than conventional film projectors, standing over 5.5 feet tall and nearly 6.5 feet long, weighing around two tons. They also use high-powered xenon lamps that require separate cooling systems.Unlike digital projection systems, 70mm IMAX projectors are no longer manufactured at scale. As the film industry transitioned to digital formats, many of the companies that produced components and the expertise required to maintain them also disappeared.Describing the challenge, Redshark News wrote,As a result, IMAX now refurbishes and upgrades existing projectors instead of building new ones.The equipment is only one part of the challenge. A feature-length 70mm IMAX print is significantly larger than conventional film reels. Individual sections are shipped separately to cinemas before being hand-spliced together over several hours into a single reel.A 2.5-hour IMAX film print stretches nearly 10 miles, weighs about 550 pounds and costs approximately $36,000 to produce. Sinceruns for nearly three hours, its print is even longer.Any failure in the projection system can be difficult to repair because replacement parts and technicians familiar with the equipment are limited. This combination of ageing machinery, specialised engineering and declining manufacturing capacity has left only 41 theatres worldwide capable of presentingin its intended 70mm IMAX format.
Article Summary: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey is only available in 41 theatres worldwide. This is due to a lack of new projector manufacturing. IMAX must rebuild and retrofit its old machines, which are large and complex. The film prints themselves are also massive, weighing hundreds of pounds.

Article Title: First time in 22 years, Google burns through $6 billion in cash; and CFO Anat Ashkenazi has further 'warning' on cash flow remaining under pressure
Article Text:
Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai

Alphabet CFO issues cash flow warning as AI CapEx soars



‘Full-steam ahead for Gemini 4’: Pichai



For the first time since going public over two decades ago, Google burned through cash in the second quarter. The shift underscores the tech giant’s massive push into artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. Alphabet reported that its free cash flow for the three months ending in June plunged to minus $5.9 billion, falling far below Wall Street expectations. The cash deficit was driven by another major hike in its budget for data centres, custom chips and specialised AI hardware.Google CFO Anat Ashkenazi raised the company’s 2026 capital expenditure (CapEx) forecast to $195 billion to $205 billion – up from earlier guidance of $180 billion to $190 billion. Ashkenazi warned investors that cash reserves will remain squeezed as the company continues to spend aggressively to capture market share.“We expect that free cash flow will remain under pressure driven by our investments in technical infrastructure, which enable us to capitalise on the AI opportunity and continue to drive attractive returns,” Ashkenazi stated during the earnings call.Google is locked in an AI arms race alongside rivals Microsoft, Meta and Amazon.Combined, the four tech giants are on track to spend over $725 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026 alone, reports have said. To fund this massive buildout, Alphabet has taken on nearly $100 billion in debt and raised roughly $85 billion in its first share sale in over twenty years.Google CEO Sundar Pichai reaffirmed the company’s commitment to leading the global AI landscape, telling investors that Google is allocating massive computing power toward training its next flagship frontier model, Gemini 4.“It feels like we are in very early innings of what feels like a secular shift across multiple areas. Over the past year, we’ve gotten more bullish on the opportunities ahead,” Pichai told investors. Google also said that there’s a commercial cloud backlog climbing to $514 billion, maintaining that the cash burn is a necessary trade-off to secure a dominant position in the evolving AI era.
Article Summary: Alphabet CFO issues cash flow warning as AI CapEx soars. Google burned through cash in the second quarter for the first time since going public over two decades ago. The shift underscores the tech giant’s massive push into artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.
